findings.passage: “It is somewhat surprising to me that the ability for that to happen in Massachusetts is possible because it is easy for us to say in Massachusetts to say ‘Our gun laws are stricter, it could never happen here,’ but we need to face the fact that it could happen here,” Farley-Bouvier says.
findings.note: Quoted by WAMC after the Las Vegas shooting, speaking about bump stocks being legal in Massachusetts. The same story says she was co-sponsoring bills with another representative to outlaw the purchase of bump stocks and high-capacity magazines.

findings.passage: State Representative Tricia Farley-Bouvier, a Pittsfield Democrat, says "bump stocks," which the Las Vegas shooter used to convert a semi-automatic rifle into what she calls "essentially [an] automatic weapon,” are legal in Massachusetts.
findings.note: WAMC reporter's wording; only the quoted phrase 'essentially [an] automatic weapon' is her own. Shows she described bump stocks as turning a rifle into an automatic weapon.

She is named as a petitioner (co-sponsor) on House docket 4266, 'An Act prohibiting large capacity feeding devices and devices that increase the rate of discharge of a weapon', filed 10/4/2017; lead filer is another representative. Co-sponsorship recorded as sponsor.
